purpose: Maps the words the market uses onto the facts the engine needs. Terms map to FACTS, never directly to categories - a term is a signal to ask a question, never an answer.
status: DRAFT, built from the tranche 1-3 collection. Extend as real product documents are read.
usage: Use signals to PRIORITISE questions, not to infer answers. A term appearing in a product description raises the question; the user still answers it.
Never let a signal set a fact value. That would be exactly the keyword matching both source reports warn against.
Trap terms are the inverse: they predict where users and documents will mislead, and where a 'why do we ask this?' explanation is most needed.

trap_terms.smart meter: Suggests Annex IV category 2. A meter is not a gateway, and the category describes gateways. See WTR-01 vs WTR-02.
trap_terms.gateway: Used loosely for any IoT hub or protocol converter. Annex IV category 2 means a smart metering gateway with specific functions. An 'IoT gateway' is usually not one.
trap_terms.camera: Suggests III-I-17. The category requires protecting the physical security of consumers in a residential setting, not the presence of a lens. See RAT-01 vs RAT-02.
trap_terms.security: Appears in product names and marketing for products with no security core functionality. Name is not evidence.
trap_terms.SOAR: Marketed with the same correlation vocabulary as SIEM, but the FAQ states SOAR is generally not SIEM because its core functionality differs.
trap_terms.critical: Three distinct meanings: Annex IV critical product, NIS 2 critical infrastructure, and everyday emphasis. See the terminology section of the case catalogue.
trap_terms.industrial: Both source reports assumed Annex III Class II firewalls carry an 'intended for industrial use' condition. No such condition exists in the official text.
trap_terms.residential and Airbnb: Observed verbatim in smart-lock marketing. Short-term rental is neither an ordinary home nor a commercial building; the honest answer is CONFLICTING. See LOCK-04.
trap_terms.smart home: A marketing bracket, not a legal one. Only III-I-16 and III-I-17 use the residential condition, and each has further conditions.
trap_terms.AI-powered: Does not by itself engage the AI Act overlap. Art. 12 applies only to high-risk AI systems under Art. 6 of Reg. 2024/1689. See AI-04.
trap_terms.secure by design: A design claim, not a statement of core functionality or of any decisive condition.
trap_terms.cloud: May indicate remote data processing that is part of the product (Art. 3(2)), or an unrelated service. The test is whether its absence would prevent a product function.
